__readme: Golden corpus for the canonical eval run decision summary (EVAL_RUN_DECISION_SUMMARY_SCHEMA_VERSION 1). ONE file, five consumers: the contract test (sdk/tests/eval-run-decision-summary.test.ts), the API route test (mcpjam-inspector/server/routes/v1/__tests__/eval-decision-summary.test.ts), the MCP operation test, the CLI reporter tests, and the structured-report renderer tests. That is the point: the API's answer, a client-side assembly, what the Platform MCP server hands a model, and what JSON/JUnit/HTML render are supposed to be ONE reading of a run, and the only way to prove it is to check all of them against the same rows. LOAD RULE: strip every key whose name starts with '__' before handing a row to a validator; they are fixture annotations and every object in this contract is closed, so a payload still carrying one would be rejected for the wrong reason. `expected` is GENERATED by running assembleEvalRunDecisionSummary over `input` and is asserted both ways: it must equal the assembler's output AND validate against evalRunDecisionSummarySchema. Regenerate it in the same PR as any change to the assembler, and read the diff — a change here is a change to what every surface says about a run. The embedded `verdictSummary` objects are copied verbatim from eval-verdict-policy-parity-fixtures.json, so the decisions this corpus explains are the same ones the verdict contract already pins.

cases.__why: A clean v2 run: the verdict is the decision's own, the counts are case-execution VARIANTS tallied from decision.cases, and there are no diagnostics because nothing failed. `scannedIterations` proves the emptiness was observed rather than assumed.

One trial per chain stage. Each diagnostic's evidence is read from the FIRST FAILED STAGE'S ROW only — the earlier stages passed and carry spans of their own, and unioning those in would present the evidence of everything that worked as the explanation of the thing that did not.

cases.__why: A setup abort and an evaluator error. Both carry a failureCategory and NEITHER carries a firstFailedStage, which is the documented shape: the run never reached a stage, so the evidence locator stays stage-less rather than inventing one to hang a link on.

cases.__why: A tool policy blocked the run. Every row is notMeasured with reason blockedByPolicy and NO failureCategory is claimed, so the next action is the honest 'go and look' fallback rather than a bucket nothing established.

items.title: Blocked by tool policy
items.nextAction: inspect the case trace; no failure category was recorded

cases.__why: Two quarantine shapes. The unverified row exposes ONLY that the chain did not validate — never firstFailedStage or failureCategory, which are claims ABOUT rows that did not validate. The version-ahead row is flagged and KEPT: a derivation from a newer analyzer is still the producer's own answer, and blanking it every time the platform ships ahead of a pinned CLI would be worse. The ahead row is stamped 99 rather than CURRENT+1 on purpose: a fixture that picks the next integer stops exercising version-ahead the moment the analyzer reaches it, which is exactly what happened when UVH-IN1 took the analyzer to 6.

cases.__why: One case, four trials, two of them failing — and the case PASSES because its pass rate meets its threshold. The counts say 1/1 case variants passed while two diagnostics are listed: diagnostics are trials beneath the aggregate and never a second tally of cases. cases.__why: Absence stays absence: a run that recorded no summary reports no counts. Defaulting them to zero would manufacture a clean bill of health out of a missing field.

A running run has concluded nothing. `notEstablished` is a fourth word precisely so this is not reported as failed (a defect nothing observed) or as inconclusive (a decision the validity phase never took).

items.nextAction: inspect the case trace; no failure category was recorded

cases.__why: A cancelled LEGACY run: its stored counts describe the iterations it happened to record, so gating on them is fail-open. A policy-v2 run is deliberately NOT resolved this way — its validity phase is where lifecycle enters the verdict.

cases.__why: Decided under policy v2 with no readable decision. There is no legacy fallback: re-deciding a v2 run under percent-threshold semantics would answer a question nobody asked. The platform's own integrity message is carried as `detail`, never synthesized.

A page reached with more to come. `complete: false` plus a cursor is the difference between 'these are the failures' and 'these are some of them' — a partial page that claimed completeness would let a reader conclude a run failed in exactly two places from a sample.
